case.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case.limits: The Court repeatedly stressed that it was addressing computer code, a form of work it called inherently functional, and disclaimed broader application. Plaintiffs read that limit narrowly and defendants read it broadly.
case.holding: Copying roughly 11,500 lines of a software interface to let developers reuse what they already knew was fair use. The Court assumed copyrightability and decided the case on fair use instead.
case.case_name: Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc.
case.why_ai_cites_it: The most recent Supreme Court fair use decision favouring a technology defendant, and the source of the argument that copying to build a platform others can create on top of weighs toward fair use.
